investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T03:26–03:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM provisioning or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect. The eval failure is an observability signal of this infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet, so impact to end users cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no remaining allocatable slots for new remote agent pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] The 4 remaining cluster nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for the kata peer-pods runtime class, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
[Possible] A prior remote agent workload (from a previous eval run, a user session, or a background job) was not cleaned up and is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new allocations.
[Possible] The kata peer-pods node pool was scaled down or a node became NotReady, reducing available vm-resource capacity below the minimum needed to schedule one additional pod.
[Lower likelihood] A node affinity/selector misconfiguration on the remote agent pod spec is excluding nodes that should be eligible, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T03:29–03:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), violating its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agent pod attempted during the eval window. The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource — required for peer-pod / confidential-VM-backed remote agents — is exhausted on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot free capacity because no lower-priority victims exist. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, so no evidence is written and the contract validation fails for all four required fields.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrent or recently-created remote agent pods have consumed the full VM slot allocation on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving no capacity for the eval pod. Preemption is also blocked (no victims found), indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If the cluster was recently scaled or nodes were replaced/relabeled, the eligible node count may have dropped, reducing total VM capacity.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level VM quota or resource limit: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource may have a hard quota set at the namespace or cluster level that is lower than the number of concurrent remote agents currently running, causing new pods to be rejected even if node-level capacity nominally exists.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner misconfiguration causing wrong node selector: the pod spec submitted by createAgent may carry an overly restrictive affinity that excludes nodes it should be able to use. This would be a code-level issue in the runner, but the scheduler message is consistent with a legitimate capacity exhaustion rather than a misconfigured selector, and all three sibling checks hit the same error.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T03:26–03:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM provisioning or readiness steps.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect. The eval failure is an observability signal of this infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet, so impact to end users cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 03:29 and 03:34 UTC on 2026-07-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api had exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~140–145 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting real infrastructure unavailability for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and 'No preemption victims found', meaning no existing pods could be evicted to free capacity (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Tertiary: A concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new pods from scheduling — this is consistent with all three sibling checks failing in sequence within the same ~5-minute window.

Lower confidence: A change to node affinity labels or kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limits on the cluster nodes could have reduced effective capacity, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
